message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated American composers—spanning from the early 19th‑century pioneers to modern film‑score maestros:

| Composer | Era / Style | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854–1932) | Romantic/Patriotic marches | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “Washington Post March” |
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | Jazz‑influenced classical | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris,” “Porgy & Bess” |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | Neoclassical/“American Sound” | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man,” “Rodeo” |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | Broadway, symphonic, jazz | “West Side Story,” “Candide,” “Symphonic Dances” |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910–1981) | Modernist/lyrical | “Adagio for Strings,” “Knoxville: Summer of 1915” |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | “Einstein on the Beach,” “Glassworks,” “Koyaanisqatsi” |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film scores | “Star Wars,” “Indiana Jones,” “Jurassic Park” |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalism | “Music for 18 Musicians,” “Different Trains” |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | Experimental/early modern | “The Unanswered Question,” “Concord Sonata” |
| **William Grant Still** (1895–1978) | African‑American composer, “Afro‑American Symphony” |
| **Ethel Smyth** (not American but influential in the U.S.) | Early 20th‑century opera composer | *[Note: She was British; included for context]* |

### Why These Names Stand Out

- **Historical Impact**: Sousa and Gershwin helped define an “American sound” in the early 20th century.
- **Broadway & Film**: Bernstein and Williams bridged concert hall and popular media, bringing classical music to wider audiences.
- **Modernist Innovation**: Copland, Barber, and Ives pushed harmonic boundaries while still sounding distinctly American.
- **Contemporary Influence**: Glass, Reich, and Williams continue to shape both concert repertoire and popular culture.

If you’re looking for a deeper dive into any particular composer or era, let me know!
